summary.one_liner: OpenSCAP is an open source security compliance toolkit whose `oscap` command-line tool loads, scans, validates, edits, and exports SCAP documents.
summary.what_it_does: The oscap command-line tool works with SCAP (Security Content Automation Protocol) documents. It can validate SCAP data streams and their components (XCCDF, OVAL, OCIL, CPE). It can evaluate OVAL definition files and write results, and evaluate XCCDF profiles or benchmarks, optionally using a CPE dictionary. It can also work with data stream collections by selecting a specific data stream and component. The tool generates XCCDF guides (optionally filtered by profile) and HTML-style reports from scan results. The README includes example commands for each of these tasks but does not describe the output formats in detail.
use_cases: scan systems against an XCCDF profile
generate compliance reports from scan results
how_to_run: oscap xccdf eval --profile Desktop --results xccdf-results.xml --cpe cpe-dictionary.xml scap-xccdf.xml
oscap xccdf generate guide XCCDF-FILE > XCCDF-GUIDE-FILE
oscap xccdf generate report XCCDF-RESULT-FILE > XCCDF-REPORT-FILE
notable: Implements SCAP standards for XCCDF, OVAL, OCIL, and CPE content
Validates whole SCAP data streams, checking every component inside
Can evaluate a single profile or a benchmark selected from a data stream collection
Generates guides and reports from XCCDF content and scan results
Community support via libera.chat IRC channel #openscap and a mailing list
caveats: The README states that Microsoft Windows support was officially void as of February 1, 2022
The README does not describe installation steps, so setup is not covered here
Requires SCAP content files (data streams, XCCDF, OVAL) as input; the README does not include them
